## Development context

Glider Reporter is an open-source, reproducible reporting template for
underwater oceanographic glider data. It combines community-submitted methods,
standardized field mapping, and client-side Quarto interfaces so users can
inspect and export reporting workflows without sending their data to an
external service.

The function registry records each method's source, implementation, and
originating GitHub Issue. This page reads that registry during rendering so the
bibliography remains synchronized as functions are added.

## Function citation registry

```{ojs}
references_registry = JSON.parse(
  await FileAttachment("functions/registry.json").text()
)
```

```{ojs}
references_bibliography = html`<ol class="references-bibliography">
  ${references_registry.map((entry) => html`<li id=${`reference-${entry.id}`}>
    <strong>${entry.citation || "Citation not provided."}</strong><br>
    Reporting function:
    <a href=${entry.code_file}>${entry.name}</a>
    (${entry.language}).
    <a href=${entry.issue_url}>GitHub Issue</a>
  </li>`)}
</ol>`
```

## AI governance disclosure

GitHub Copilot and other large-language-model assistants may be used to help
develop and maintain this project. Their use can include drafting code and
documentation, suggesting tests, explaining failures, and supporting review.
AI-generated suggestions are treated as untrusted contributions: maintainers
review the proposed changes, run available tests and builds, and retain
responsibility for scientific accuracy, security, licensing, accessibility,
and final publication decisions.

AI assistance does not replace domain expertise or peer review. Scientific
methods and reporting functions should remain traceable through citations,
source files, and GitHub Issues so users can evaluate their provenance and
limitations. Contributors should not place confidential data, credentials, or
other sensitive information in prompts or committed files.
